summary: The article profiles Socceroos coach Graham Arnold as he prepares to break the record for most matches as national team manager, against Bangladesh in 2026 World Cup qualifying. It traces how he survived intense criticism in March 2022, credited largely to his bold substitution of Mat Ryan for Andrew Redmayne in the Peru playoff. It also covers Football Australia's praise, Arnold's reflections, and the qualification format.
one_line: Graham Arnold is set to become the Socceroos' record-holder for matches as coach, a milestone owed to his bold goalkeeper switch against Peru.
key_facts: In March 2022 Graham Arnold seemed a 'dead man walking' as the Socceroos' World Cup qualification campaign lurched towards failure.
Australia finished seven points off automatic qualification for Qatar after one win in seven games, leaving a playoff against United Arab Emirates and then Peru.
Football Australia stuck by Arnold, likely due to the lateness of the hour and financial considerations rather than overwhelming faith.
Australia qualified and bowed out of the Qatar World Cup to eventual champions Argentina after nearly taking them to extra time.
Arnold dismissed critics such as Mark Bosnich and Craig Foster with a blunt 'who cares?'.
With moments left in extra time against Peru, Arnold replaced Mat Ryan with Andrew Redmayne, who saved the decisive spot kick.
Arnold will coach his 59th match on Thursday against Bangladesh, taking him clear of Frank Farina.
Arnold played for the Socceroos 56 times and has been in national team coaching since 2000, as assistant to Farina and then Guus Hiddink, plus caretaker coach in 2006.
FA CEO James Johnson said 'Anyone who knows Arnie will tell you he bleeds green and gold.'
FIFA is expanding the World Cup from 36 to 48 teams, so eight direct Asian qualifiers will advance instead of four.
Australia opens at AAMI Park in Melbourne on Thursday night, then plays Palestine in the Middle East next Wednesday (1.00am AEDT).
The qualifying stage has nine groups of four, with Lebanon the other team in Group I; the top two from each go to three groups of six running September 2024 to June 2025.
